title: Perfect tenses with έχω
goal: Form and use the perfect and pluperfect, active and passive.

blocks.text:
The perfect is **έχω + the non-finite form**, which is identical to the 3rd singular of the perfective: θα γράψει → **έχω γράψει**; passive θα γραφτεί → **έχει γραφτεί**. The pluperfect swaps in είχα: **είχα γράψει**.

Use is narrower than in English. Greek prefers the simple past for finished events, even recent ones (Το είδες; 'Have you seen it?'), and keeps the perfect for a past event whose result matters now or experiences up to now (Έχω πάει στην Κρήτη τρεις φορές). For 'I have lived here for two years', Greek uses the present: Μένω εδώ δύο χρόνια.

blocks.title: Τα 'χω χάσει: idioms built on the perfect
blocks.text: Everyday Greek has a set of idioms in the perfect, usually with **τα** 'them' and the elided **'χω** for έχω. **Τα 'χω χάσει** 'I'm completely confused' (lit. 'I have lost them'). **Τα 'χουν φτιάξει** 'they're going out together' (lit. 'they have fixed them'). **Τα 'κανες θάλασσα** 'you've made a mess of it' (lit. 'you made them sea'). The perfect also opens one of the commonest greetings between friends: **Πού έχεις χαθεί;** 'where have you been hiding?'. And note **έχω να** + dependent for 'it's been a while since': **Έχω να σε δω δύο χρόνια** 'I haven't seen you for two years'.

blocks.title: Μετά από έξι χρόνια
blocks.en:
— Marina! I don't believe it! Where have you been hiding?
— Giorgos! How long has it been since we saw each other... five years?
— Six. The last time I saw you, you had just finished university and you were getting ready to leave for Barcelona.
— Yes, and in the end I stayed there four years. Last year I came back to Thessaloniki. What about you? What have you been doing all this time?

— Lots! I've changed jobs three times, I've moved house twice, I've learned to cook and... I've got married!
— Really? Congratulations! Do I know her?
— Sofia, from secondary school. We had lost touch for years and we met again by chance at a concert. Have you met anyone?
— Not yet. I haven't found time even for a holiday! I've opened a small translation office and I work all the time.
— And Barcelona? Have you been back since?
— Not yet, but I'm planning to go in May. I've really missed my friends there.

— Good for you! You always wanted to do something of your own. Have you been to the new café on the square?
— No, I haven't. Is it good?
— The best! Come on, let's go now. I've got lots to tell you, and I want you to tell me about Barcelona too.

gloss.Έχουμε: έχω να + dependent — it's been (a while) since: Έχουμε να βρεθούμε = we haven't seen each other for
gloss.λείψει: λείπω — (have) been missed: μου έχουν λείψει = I've missed
gloss.επαγγελματικά: επαγγελματικά — professionally, in terms of work

questions.prompt: Πόσα χρόνια είχαν να βρεθούν η Μαρίνα και ο Γιώργος;
Πού έζησε η Μαρίνα μετά τη σχολή;
Πού ξανασυναντήθηκαν ο Γιώργος και η Σοφία;
Τι έχει κάνει η Μαρίνα επαγγελματικά;

items.why: Non-finite = 3sg perfective: θα πάει.

items.prompt: Όταν έφτασα, το τρένο είχε ήδη ___. (φεύγω)
I have lived here for two years.
items.why: Ongoing state up to now: present.

items.prompt: Το γράμμα έχει ___ ήδη. (passive of γράφω)

items.why: The non-finite form = 3sg dependent: θα φάει → έχω φάει.
βλέπω → θα δει → έχω δει.
πηγαίνω/πάω → θα πάει → έχουμε πάει; experience up to now.

items.prompt: Όταν φτάσαμε, η ταινία είχε ήδη ___ (αρχίζω).
items.why: Earlier than another past event: pluperfect είχε + non-finite.
Passive non-finite = passive 3sg dependent: θα σταλεί → έχει σταλεί.
θα πουληθεί → έχει πουληθεί.
The result matters now (I can't log in): perfect.
καταλαβαίνω → θα καταλάβει → έχετε καταλάβει.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *Have you ever been to Crete?*
items.why: Experience up to now: perfect with ποτέ.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *I haven't finished yet.*
items.why: δεν goes before έχω; ακόμα/ακόμη 'yet'.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *She had already left.*
items.why: Pluperfect: είχε + φύγει.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *We have been living here since 2020.*
items.why: A state still going on takes the present in Greek, not the perfect.
A specific past time (πέρσι) rules out the perfect: simple past.

items.prompt: ___ αυτό το βιβλίο τρεις φορές μέχρι τώρα.
items.why: μέχρι τώρα 'so far': experience up to the present, perfect.
Already completed before a past moment: pluperfect.
πότε asks for a point in time, so the simple past is used.
εδώ και + present = 'for (and still)'; πριν από means 'ago'.
Completed before a future moment: future perfect θα έχω + non-finite.
